title: Theorem 4.4: local structure of closed immersions into affine spectral Deligne-Mumford stacks
statement_scope: Let A be a connective E∞-ring and let f:(X,O)→Spec A be a map of spectral Deligne-Mumford stacks. Then f is a closed immersion if and only if there exists an equivalence (X,O)≃Spec B for which the induced map A→B induces a surjection π0A→π0B. The whole theorem and both directions are retained.
difficulty_reason: Rule author-work-bearing-core-v1-20261114: this is a substantial research-bearing local-structure theorem, proving both that a surjection on π0 gives a closed immersion and that every closed immersion into Spec A is affine of the form Spec B with π0A→π0B surjective; the argument uses the closed-immersion lemmas, quasi-coherent pushforward, t-exactness and a final comparison of ∞-topoi (statement page 20; proof page 22). Clearly beyond routine qualifying-exam work.

difficulty_evidence.bearing_core: Local structure theorem identifying closed immersions into affine spectral Deligne-Mumford stacks with maps Spec B→Spec A inducing a surjection on π0.
